newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB says debt provisions prudent.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB says debt provisions prudent.

text.p: National Australia Bank (NAB) on Thursday defended a large increase in its provisions for doubtful debt last financial year, describing the move as prudent banking practise, rather than taking on "unsatisfactory exposures".

"Our credit assessment people have taken the view that the Australian economy in quite a number of areas is not performing strongly and we felt it was prudent banking practice...," chairman William Irvine told the group's annual meeting.
"It's a prudent provisioning exercise. It certainly does not reflect the taking on of any unsatisfactory exposures," he said.
He said economic conditions were also soft in the United Kingdom where NAB's owns the Yorkshire Bank and the Clydesdale Bank in England.

"Economic conditions have deteriorated over the year so we had to step in...to tighten up their credit provisioning, so that's the only reason why the bottom line result is Yorkshire stand out against other banks, but generaly speaking they are doing very well," Irvine said.
NAB's operating profit in its United Kingdom and Ireland banking and financial services group fell four percent to A$403 million in the year to September 30, 1996.
NAB's total provision for doubtful debts rose to A$173.71 million in the year to September 30, from A$148.12 million in the previous year.
The bank's net profit rose 6.6 percent to A$2.10 billion in 1995/96.
